P01.passage: Every spring until 1914, the people of one moorland village set out together at dawn, crossed six miles of open common to its far edge, and came home by dusk. At the boundary stone the young men, faces blackened with soot, crossed into the neighboring parish, cut down the maypole its people had raised on their green, and fought off the neighbors who ran out to stop them. Folklorists who recorded the walk in 1900 called it the village's yearly ______. They ran home past the grazing ponies with the pole on their shoulders, and it was burned that night on the village green.
P01.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P02.passage: Beside a rail line, a strip of uncut grass a few yards wide runs twelve miles across plowed farmland between two forests, and meadow voles live in both forests. Two decades of trapping suggest that the strip has served as the voles' ______. Young voles pushed out of crowded forest edges settle in the strip's seed-heavy grass within a few hundred yards of where they entered, and owls hunt it from the line's poles. Within a month, tags of over half the voles marked there turn up in pellets beneath the poles, while voles that wander back to the forest edge live as long as those that never left.
P02.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P03.passage: For two centuries a flock of sheep has grazed one slope of a narrow valley in the hills, while a stone wall along the stream has kept them off the opposite slope. The flock crops its slope evenly from top to bottom, holding the turf an inch high, with tiny flowers blooming low among it, while across the stream brambles and tall tussocks crowd the ground. The soil tests no richer than the ungrazed slope's, and the sheep wander the slope in every direction, leaving no worn paths. Comparing the two slopes, one ecologist concluded that the flock had ______ its hillside.
P03.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P04.passage: Two geologists measured the stones of a steep river running eight miles from granite and sandstone cliffs to the sea. Their report argued that the river had ______ those stones, and its photographs set out the case. Sieved, the bed was nearly all oven-sized boulders at the cliffs, fist-sized cobbles four miles down, and pea gravel at the sea. Painted stones moved a mile downstream with each flood, lying wherever they stopped. A stone cracked open showed the same shade inside as out. Even at the sea, broken pebbles still fit back together edge to edge.
P04.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P05.passage: Twice a day the tide floods a salt marsh where a farm creek meets a bay, then drains it through one channel. For two years a team compared the water leaving by that channel with the water that had entered. The outgoing water ran as brown with mud as what came in and carried as much fertilizer nitrate as the creek brings down. On sunny afternoons it held half again as much oxygen as the bay. The team's report calls the marsh the bay's ______. In late summer, when the bay's deep water runs short of oxygen, fish crowd the channel's mouth on every afternoon ebb.
P05.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P06.passage: A woolen mill stood on a hill trout stream from 1840 until 1930, and the next year a fisheries officer walked the stream from source to river. Through the mill yard the miller lined both banks with cut stone for a quarter mile, so the stream that had wandered among gravel bars and alder roots ran straight between them. The wheel turned in that quick current, and the whole stream ran past it. Trout below the mill were as many as above it. His report judged that in ninety years the mill had ______ the stream.
P06.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P07.passage: Twenty thousand years ago a glacier half a mile thick filled a mountain valley, and it lay there for several thousand years. When it melted, it spread clay, sand and stones forty feet deep from wall to wall, and the floor's surface is now smooth enough to plow. Wells dug anywhere on the floor pass through that layer before reaching granite, whose old crumbling crust from before the ice is still there. That glacier, geologists agree, ______ the valley floor. The river winds across the farms in a shallow bed it has cut no deeper than ten feet.
P07.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P08.passage: In 1760 a riverside landowner built a brick wall twelve feet high and a quarter mile long beside his orchard, near a village of thatched cottages. It runs along the orchard's northern edge, open at both ends, and the river runs past the orchard's southern edge, with the village on its far bank. Peaches trained on the wall's sunny face set fruit in springs when frost blackens every other blossom, and the bricks there stay warm to the hand at midnight. A fire in 1791 burned the village to the ground and never crossed the water. Estate letters of the next fifty years treat the wall as the orchard's ______.
P08.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P09.passage: In 1859 a merchant built a log store at a mountain gold camp, the only building there with a stove, an iron safe and a shelf of bottles, and his ledger survives. It lists watches, pistols and a fiddle that miners left in his safe against credit for flour and powder; most were redeemed when their owners struck pay dirt, and each fall he sold the rest. One historian of the camp called the store, in those years, the camp's ______. The bottles held whiskey, and he banked the stove and barred the door at sundown.
P09.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P10.passage: A city turned a forty-acre rail yard into a park, with a highway on its north edge and, to the south, row houses and apartment towers that the yard had divided for a century. Its lawns slope open to the highway, and paved paths run across it from both neighborhoods to a footbridge leading over the highway to a train station. Gate counts found thirty thousand people a day on those paths, most of them local residents at rush hour, few lingering past the ten minutes the walk takes. A study of the park's first decade called it the district's ______. Its benches stand mostly empty at midday.
P10.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P11.passage: For a decade the old salt mine served the nearby city's art museum as its ______. The mine's chambers lie six hundred feet down, where the air stays cool and dry all year, and a single lift shaft reaches them. The museum hung its paintings uncrated along the walls of the largest chamber, under electric lamps, and the lift carried hundreds of townspeople down each Sunday to walk past them. The paintings stayed there unchanged, and every one went back up when the museum's new building opened.
P11.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P12.passage: In 1690 a merchant ship carrying iron bars and wine sank in sixty feet of water off a rocky coast. The water there is warm and rich in oxygen, and when divers reached the wreck in 1990 its hull still stood upright on the open bottom, its outline whole and its cargo in the hold. Every plank they lifted crumbled in their hands into a lace of pencil-wide tunnels. The divers' report says that three centuries of seawater had ______ the ship. From a few yards away, the hull looked as sound as on the day it sank.
P12.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P13.passage: In 1960 a dam was built across a mountain river, holding back a reservoir three hundred feet deep. Twenty years of surveys show that the dam has ______ the river below it. Its turbines run only in the afternoons, when demand for power peaks, drawing water from just beneath the reservoir's sunlit surface. Each afternoon the river below rises four feet within an hour; by midnight it has dropped to a trickle between dry gravel bars, and it stays there until the turbines start again. The bars shift from week to week, and bass still spawn just below the dam.
P13.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P14.passage: For thirty years beavers have lived on a creek in a dry mountain valley; the creek in the next valley has none. The beavers' dams are low heaps of sticks that each spring's runoff washes out, and the creek runs in the same shallow, stony bed as next door. For two hundred yards up both slopes, where aspens once grew as thickly as across the ridge, only gnawed stumps remain. A hydrologist who has studied both valleys concludes that the beavers have ______ theirs. In dry summers both valleys turn the same brown.
P14.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P15.passage: A clay tablet dug from the ruins of an ancient river city lists barley in nine lines, each giving an amount followed by a word or two, and a seal has been rolled across its back. Each line pairs an amount with a word, barley, dates, water, then barley again marked sprouted and then crushed, and the fifth line adds three days; a second column repeats every amount exactly doubled, and the seal is the temple brewer's. The tablet lay among the brewery's jars, its corners rubbed smooth. Scholars now read the tablet as its owner's ______.
P15.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P16.passage: In 1911 a steel freighter struck a reef off a small island and sank, and its hull still lies there, nearly whole. Divers who surveyed it in 2005 called the hull a true ______, and their photographs show why. Its ribs and plates, in forty feet of clear water, are grown over with corals and sponges along every beam, while the flat sand around it holds almost none. All thirty of its crew rowed ashore in the ship's boats, and its cargo was coal, left in the holds where it fell. The island's ferries pass over it twice a day.
P16.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P17.passage: From 1952 to 1957 almost no rain fell on a pine forest in the southern hills, where foresters measured every tree yearly until 1975. Through every dry summer the pines kept green needles while the soil shrank away from their roots. After the autumn gales of 1955 and 1956, one tree in five lay on the ground, roots in the air beside the pit they had torn open, most of them the tallest and soundest pines on the ridges. Once the rains returned, the standing pines put on growth rings as wide as before 1952. The foresters' final report concluded that the dry years had ______ the forest.
P17.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P18.passage: For three summers an entomologist watched garden ants tend aphids on a row of beans, lapping up the honeydew the aphids release. The aphids stayed on whatever shoot they had settled on, wilting or not, and walked as quickly on leaves the workers had crossed as on clean ones. As the beans withered in autumn, workers carried the aphids' eggs down into the nest, and a nest dug up in midwinter held thousands of them heaped in its deepest chamber. Her report concludes that the ants had ______ the aphids. In spring the eggs hatched there, and the young aphids climbed out to the new bean shoots.
P18.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P19.passage: During a two-year war in the 1870s, one small country's government changed how it dealt with the country's four daily newspapers. Their editors joined a press committee that met weekly with the war ministry, and the four dailies ran its recruiting appeals free of charge and printed the casualty lists it supplied. The papers stayed in private hands, their sales climbing. No censor read their pages. One historian's account of those years says the government ______ the press. In their own columns the editors urged readers to enlist, and they dropped the peace appeals they had carried before the war.
P19.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P20.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1996, biologists began counting its one elk herd each winter and tracking collared elk year-round. Over the following decade, the wolves ______ the herd. By 2006 the river meadows held as many elk in winter as ever, collared cows kept to their old ranges, and on film the elk grazed heads down as long as before 1996. The carcasses found at wolf kills were mostly old cows with worn teeth and elk lame from hoof rot, and with fewer mouths competing for winter grass, more calves lived to spring, holding the count near 900.
P20.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P21.passage: In 1990 conservators began a ten-year survey of a ruined castle wall, half of which had been cloaked in ivy for two centuries. The ivy's leaves overlap like shingles down the wall's face. Moisture readings in the stone behind them were a third of those on the bare half, where rain soaks in and freezes each winter. Stones on both halves stood firm in sound mortar, and stone faces under the stems were clean. The survey's final report says that the ivy had ______ the wall. A gale in the survey's eighth year left both halves standing.
P21.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P22.passage: On one island a thorny shrub with hollow thorns and nectar glands houses ants on nearly every plant. For three years an ecologist kept the ants off some shrubs with sticky bands and compared them with their neighbors. The ants spent the day inside the thorns, coming out after dark to drink at the glands, while caterpillars fed in daylight and chewed banded and unbanded shrubs alike. In those three years, the ants ______ the shrub. Freed of them, banded shrubs flowered and podded as heavily, their seeds dropped beneath them as their neighbors' did, and they grew a third taller.
P22.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P23.passage: For two centuries after 1700, the dunes of a desert basin pressed against a walled oasis village of mud-brick houses and date palms. Every decade the nearest dune crept a few dozen yards into the gardens on the village's western edge and buried palms to their crowns. As the sand reached their walls, families on that side gave up their houses one at a time and rebuilt a lane farther east, on the same level ground. Caravans kept reaching the eastern gate the whole time. In those two centuries, the sand had ______ the village.
P23.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P24.passage: In 1951 the last congregation left a stone church that had stood at the center of a river town since 1720. Engineers that winter found its walls sound and its tower true. That spring the river flooded the lower town, and the council, over the objections of the church's trustees, moved two hundred families' furniture and the town's emergency grain into the nave, where they stayed for three years. In 1955 the trustees got their church back, unaltered. The town's minutes record that in 1952 the council ______ the church.
P24.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P25.passage: In 1902 a woman published the prairie diary her mother had kept from 1858 to 1871, and the mother's notebooks now sit in a state archive. Scholars who set the book beside the notebooks in 1990 found that the daughter had ______ the diary. Line by line the book follows the notebooks, misspellings like "chickins" and "sumer" included, down to the weekly egg tallies, and nothing in it comes from outside them. Where the mother cursed her husband after a quarrel, the book reads "my husband was tired today," and the winter she wrote of leaving him reads "a hard winter."
P25.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P26.passage: In 1890 a novel about a fishing family on a bleak northern coast, written in a small country's language, appeared in its first English translation. The translator kept the family's names, its fjord, its money and every chapter in order, and his sentences follow the original's short, abrupt rhythm clause by clause. In a handful of scenes he changed a few lines: the three drownings end in rescues at the last moment, and the youngest child, who starves in the original's second winter, is carried through it by a neighbor's gift of flour. Set beside the original line by line, the translation shows that its translator ______ the novel.
P26.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P27.passage: In 1790 a merchant ship carrying iron bars and casks of wine sank in thirty feet of water off a sandy coast that storms strike every winter. Two centuries on the seabed had ______ the ship, according to the divers who surveyed it in 1990. Its iron bars and casks lie strewn over half a mile of open sand, in a line running the way the winter storms blow. Oak planks turn up all along that line, rolled along the bottom each winter and scoured smooth and pale, their wood still heavy and sound.
P27.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P28.passage: In 1851 a young poet paid a printer in her city to issue three hundred copies of her first collection, on terms that gave her a share of every copy sold. Within months a printer in another city issued the same poems, word for word and with her name on the title page, at half her price, paying her nothing, and his copies filled the shops that stocked hers, where hers stopped selling. The city papers had already named two of the poems among the season's best, and the two editions together came to barely four hundred copies. Within two years, her poems had been ______.
P28.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P29.passage: From 1400 to 1700 a monastery stood on a ledge above the only road through a mountain valley, and its account books survive. Each year they list dozens of guests who stayed for months, townspeople with coughs sent up by doctors for the dry air, paying board by the month, and beside most names a monk wrote the date they went home well. Guests came only with a doctor's letter, and drovers on the road were sent on to the village inn. The monks bought their prayer books from a printer in the city. In those books, one historian has argued, the monastery appears as the valley's ______.
P29.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P30.passage: In 1987 a forty-ton whale died at sea and sank two miles to a seafloor where food is otherwise scarce. A biologist who has filmed it since 1988 calls the carcass the seafloor's ______. For six years the same few sleeper sharks, known by their scars, came back every few weeks, each tearing off a mouthful or two of the cold flesh before swimming away. Between their visits the carcass lay untouched, no animal living on it, and its last flesh was not taken until 1994.
P30.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P31.passage: In 1789 a fleet of eleven sailing ships left port carrying settlers along a coast of sandy bays and rocky headlands. In its third week at sea, the weather ______ several of the fleet's ships. For nine days five of them lay within sight of one another and of the same headland, canvas hanging from the yards, on water so still that scraps thrown from the galleys floated beside the hulls until dark. The crews cut the water ration twice, and on the tenth morning all five reached harbor a week late, with not a spar broken.
P31.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P32.passage: In the second year of the war, the northern alliance ______ the island's only port. Before the war the port had shipped wool to buyers on both sides of the strait. That spring the island's wool, until then half of all the wool the alliance imported, vanished from the alliance's markets, while freighters bound for neutral countries loaded more of it at the port than ever. The waterfront sheds stood as before, no alliance warship came near the harbor, and the island's flag went on flying over the customs house.
P32.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P33.passage: One spring the river rose over its banks and stood on a farmer's lowest field for nine days. The field is a dense clay, and the water, clear from a reservoir upstream, sat on it until the sun took it. Planting, done there most years in early spring, waited until midsummer, when the ground would at last bear a tractor's weight. Walking the field in late summer, the county's soil scientist said that the flood had ______ it. Her samples showed the same nitrogen in the top foot of soil as before the flood, and the clay's surface had dried into hard, cracked plates.
P33.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P34.passage: In 1590 a printer issued an engraved chart of a stretch of coast, copied from a navy surveyor's hand-drawn map. The print is the survey's size, with north at the top of both, and its open sea is as bare of ornament as the surveyor left it. Every cape and bay matches the survey exactly except at the mouth of the navy's harbor. There the channel runs half a mile east of the surveyor's line, across a reef, and two shoals block the channel he drew. Foreign captains bought it by the hundred. Setting the two side by side, a historian found that the engraver had ______ the survey.
P34.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P35.passage: A two-lane road laid across a valley floor in 1960 carried loaded logging trucks for thirty years, and surveyors checked it each fall against stakes along its shoulders. Each July its asphalt softened in the heat, and at the stop sign below the long climb, where loaded trucks braked hard all day, it was shoved forward into folds crossing both lanes, each a stride from the next. The stakes showed the roadbed at the height it was laid, the asphalt on the climb, where trucks crawled in the same wheel tracks, stayed level, and nowhere did it crack. By 1990, its surface had been ______.
P35.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P36.passage: A glacier fills the head of a high valley whose river runs past farming villages to the plain. The only road over the mountains leaves the valley at its lower end, miles below the ice. Since the 1700s its front has crept down the valley in every cold decade and drawn back in every warm one. Most of its meltwater sinks into deep gravel, so the river past the villages hardly changes between morning and night and in dry summers runs as low as the plain's rain-fed streams. A study of three centuries of village records describes the glacier as the valley's ______.
P36.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P37.passage: A lone coral outcrop the size of a small car rises from the sand of a shallow lagoon, a quarter mile inside the reef that rings it. By day, snappers and groupers from the outer reef arrive one at a time and hang head-down beside it, gill covers flared, while shrimp living in its crevices crawl over them and feed. Each fish swims back to the reef within minutes. On a nearby reef where divers removed every shrimp, groupers now carry three times as many parasites as groupers that make the trip to the outcrop. Divers who have logged its visitors since 1985 call the outcrop the lagoon's ______.
P37.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P38.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1995, a pack of nine settled along the creek where a herd of four hundred elk spends each winter. Over the decade that followed, the pack ______ the herd. In deep snow the wolves spread out in a wide arc on the open benches and walked slowly toward the elk, which moved off ahead of them downhill into a side canyon where drifts lay chest-deep; there, floundering, several fell in an afternoon to wolves trotting on the crust. By spring the elk were back grazing the benches and the willows along the creek.
P38.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P39.passage: A sandbar lies across the river mouth below the old port, twelve feet under water at high tide and bare at low tide. Harbor records from the 1800s show the bar serving as the port's ______ for most of a century. The channel over it was a single ship wide, so arriving ships anchored outside and crossed one behind another, each logged by name and hour by the watchman on the point. The duties on their cargo were paid later, at the customs house beside the town's piers, where ships tied up to unload. In winter gales the ocean swells rolled over the bar and broke against those piers.
P39.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P40.passage: In 1797 an occupying army entered a port city whose museum held some four hundred paintings and bronzes, many of them carried off from neighboring towns by the city's own fleet a century earlier. Its officers crated every painting and bronze, listed each against a number, and stacked the crates under guard in the harbor fort, and the commander sent the council a copy of the list with a sum written beneath the total. When the council's bankers delivered that sum the next spring, the crates went back to the museum with their seals unbroken. Within a year, the army had ______ the museum's collection.
P40.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
